title: ASF artifact frontmatter
description: ASF 8.3 — the YAML frontmatter of the markdown artifacts under docs/. It holds only what state.json does not have: id, title and descriptive fields. Statuses, references and priorities are in state.json, and what can be computed is stored nowhere. Strict like state.json: a key not listed is an error, so a `status` in an RF, RNF, epic, task, bug or story fails. An artifact validates against the $def matching its directory: requirements/RF-* -> rf, requirements/RNF-* -> rnf, epics/ -> epic, tasks/ -> task, bugs/ -> bug, stories/ -> us, decisions/ADR-* -> adr, decisions/planning-archive.md -> archive. ADRs and the archive are not in state.json and keep their own status. The root is a pure $defs container: callers select a def with {"$ref": "#/$defs/<kind>"}.

layer.description: A layer of the project: a node of its tree that one agent can own while another works elsewhere. The names belong to the project, not to ASF: every repo of `state.json` project.repos is a layer, and so is every `.asf/architecture.json` component that declares a `path` (D-8.24).

module_id.description: Id of a module of docs/instructions.md, as its `<!-- asf:module id=… -->` marker declares it (`be-python-fastapi`). Lowercase and hyphens: no module id can be mistaken for a rule id, so the two live in the same list without ambiguity. The shape is all a schema can check — that the module is really in instructions.md is a cross-file check of validate-stack.py.

rf.description: Functional requirement — docs/requirements/RF-NNN.md. A verifiable behaviour, with acceptance criteria in BDD form. Status and priority are in state.json (`requirements.functional[]`).

title.description: Title; the first H1 of the file is `# <id> — <title>`.

attachments.description: Optional, since ASF 8.5. Files committed with the repository in the flat folder docs/attachments/ — flat because the same attachment may be cited by several artifacts. Pointers only: no size and no media type, because both are known when the file is served and in a file they would age. The name allows no spaces, since the validator's cited-path check stops at a space and would report a truncated path that does not exist.

links.description: Optional, since ASF 8.5. http(s) URLs of material that lives outside the repository — a Figma project, a Miro board. Never validated over the network: no tool reaches the network to check them. A downloaded .fig file is an ordinary attachment; the link to the Figma project is an entry here.

rnf.description: Non-functional requirement — docs/requirements/RNF-NNN.md. Status, verification signature and priority are in state.json (`requirements.non_functional[]`); its epics are those that cite it in `epics[].rnf_refs`.

title.description: Title; the first H1 of the file is `# <id> — <title>`.

category.description: Optional. What kind of quality it constrains, so that a report can group them.

metric.description: What is measured, e.g. «p95 latency of GET /projects». Optional: not every quality has a number, and inventing one is worse than saying how it is checked.

threshold.description: The value that separates satisfied from violated, e.g. «< 300 ms».

verification.description: How satisfaction is established: a test, a pipeline check, a scan, a measurement, a documented review. Required, because an unverifiable non-functional requirement is a wish.
